candidate_relations.reason: Altered mentation with basal-ganglia lesions and CSF pleocytosis is not hepatic encephalopathy from hepatitis C.
Rickettsial studies were negative.
Subacute meningoencephalitis describes the CSF/clinical syndrome without aspergillus etiology.
A statement that other infections were excluded is not a diagnosis of aspergillosis.
Later necrosis with peripheral enhancement can represent abscess, a related mass-forming infection missing Aspergillus.
Aspergillus infection is the same etiologic object as aspergillosis.
Rasmussen encephalitis is a chronic unihemispheric childhood epilepsy, not this febrile basal-ganglia infection.
Progressive CSF neutrophilia and necrotic enhancing lesions are not a metabolic encephalopathy.
Mucormycosis is a related invasive mold but a different organism from aspergillosis.
JC-virus PCR was negative and PML does not produce this neutrophilic CSF profile.
Hepatitis C-associated encephalopathy does not explain neutrophilic meningitis and necrotic basal-ganglia lesions.
CNS lymphoma is a neoplastic differential, not aspergillosis.
Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy remains excluded by the inflammatory CSF and negative JC PCR.
Subacute bacterial meningitis is a syndromic parent without Aspergillus.
CNS vasculitis is not the reference infectious diagnosis.
Quantiferon and AFB studies were negative; this is not tuberculous meningitis.
Cryptococcal meningitis typically has a different CSF profile and is not the reference aspergillosis.
A considered-but-ruled-out infection list is not aspergillosis; initial fungal studies being negative also cannot exclude it.
SSPE is a chronic measles encephalitis of children/young adults with a different course.
IV heroin use raises septic emboli from endocarditis, but TTE showed no vegetations; it is a related differential, not aspergillosis.

case_quality_flags: Brain biopsy was planned but not reported; initial CSF fungal studies were negative, which does not exclude aspergillosis.
